primary_diagnosis_treated: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) secondary to coronary artery disease

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and potassium at 1‑2 weeks, then every 6 months
medications.purpose: Disease‑modifying therapy for HFrEF; reduces mortality and hospitalisation
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 first‑line ACE‑I for all HFrEF patients

medications.duration: Lifelong — review potassium and renal function at 1‑2 weeks, then every 6 months
medications.purpose: MRA improves survival in HFrEF; added to ACE‑I and beta‑blocker
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 first‑line MRA for all HFrEF patients

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and volume status at 3 months, then annually
medications.purpose: Reduces HF hospitalisation and slows CKD progression, indicated regardless of diabetes status
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 first‑line SGLT2‑I for all HFrEF patients (TA902/TA929)

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily (or BID if needed)
medications.duration: As needed to achieve eu‑volemia; titrate in 20‑40 mg increments, review 2 weeks after any change
medications.purpose: Symptom control of fluid overload (edema, dyspnoea) in HFrEF
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 loop diuretic for fluid overload symptoms

medications.duration: Lifelong — review heart rate and blood pressure annually; consider uptitration to 150‑200 mg if HR >70 bpm and tolerated
medications.purpose: Beta‑blocker improves survival in HFrEF and provides angina control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 beta‑blocker for all stable HFrEF patients

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention after myocardial infarction and coronary artery bypass grafting
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 antiplatelet therapy for IHD

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 high‑intensity statin for IHD

medications.dose: 0.4 mg sublingual PRN for chest pain
2 mg/mL oral solution as prescribed for Alzheimer’s disease

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ACE‑I dose.
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, monitor standing BP and symptoms after each titration step.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and MRA increase risk of hyperkalaemia and renal impairment.
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and eGFR before start and 1‑2 weeks after each dose change; hold if K⁺ >5.0 mmol/L or eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m².

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect may cause volume depletion, hypotension, and renal function decline.
interactions_checked.action: If furosemide is required, start dapagliflozin after assessing volume status; consider reducing loop diuretic dose if symptomatic hypotension occurs.
Monitor BP and heart rate after initiation.

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in HFrEF (NICE NG106).
contraindications.alternative: Avoid; use alternative rate control if needed (e.g., ivabradine if sinus rhythm and HR >75 bpm).

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in HFrEF (NICE NG106).
contraindications.alternative: Avoid; consider other anti‑anginal agents such as ranolazine.

contraindications.reason: Can worsen fluid retention and renal function in HF (NICE NG106).
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain; use NSAIDs only if absolutely necessary with close monitoring.

contraindications.reason: Thiazolidinediones cause fluid retention and are contraindicated in HF (NICE NG106).
contraindications.alternative: Consider other glucose‑lowering agents (e.g., metformin if eGFR ≥30, or DPP‑4 inhibitor).

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for ACE‑I, MRA and SGLT2‑I initiation; obtain recent eGFR before starting.
Serum potassium not provided – baseline K⁺ required (<5.0 mmol/L) before starting spironolactone; repeat after dose changes.
Left‑ventricular ejection fraction not documented – diagnosis states HFrEF; confirm LVEF ≤40 % with echocardiogram.
Blood pressure not documented – baseline BP needed to ensure tolerance of ACE‑I and additional agents.
Liver function tests not provided – important given alcohol use and simvastatin; monitor ALT/AST.
Cause of anemia and leukopenia not clarified – investigate iron studies, B12/folate, occult GI bleed before considering ESA.
Potential adherence issues due to moderate‑to‑severe Alzheimer’s disease – involve carer, use pill‑organiser, simplify regimen.
treatment_summary: Start guideline‑directed medical therapy for HFrEF with ramipril, spironolactone and dapagliflozin, add a loop diuretic only if signs of congestion are present, and continue existing beta‑blocker, antiplatelet, statin, nitrate, inhalers and memantine. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, blood pressure and volume status closely, and address missing investigations (eGFR, K⁺, LVEF) before titration. Avoid contraindicated drugs such as verapamil, diltiazem, NSAIDs and pioglitazone.
